reasons.A: Plainest and most modern in movement and diction; its irony is mild and explanatory, lacking the passage's dry mock-solemn periods ('the ingratitude of republics').
reasons.B: Best catches the passage's ironic mock-dignity ('a different school of economics', 'the common fate of original thinkers') in long, balanced, periodic sentences with a measured, urbane stance.
reasons.C: Has the right ironic stance ('misunderstandings to which benefactors are always exposed'), but its many clipped short sentences break the passage's longer, rolling rhythm.
